V3-fired.v: A police body or robot counts an agent a foe for having fired only if it saw the shot (its own sight, at the time) or once the cell is placed. While a gang shooting is pending and unplaced, an agent who fired earlier and now stands holstered is not shot on sight. Drawn, seen violence, a known face and the rest of ai.intent stand as today.
V3-fired.replaces: ai.intent foe 'fired' = the agent has ever fired (Gun.Fired), which the police can't know
V3-fired.build: the minimum Keel probed: HasFoe 'fired' returns Gun.Fired && !GangPending. Measured: changes no plan but the veteran (14 plans).
V3-fired.why: Information moves through people (§01): an officer arriving at an unseen shooting doesn't know who fired. Without it V2 (the gang shooting's placing) never matters: the veteran loses enforcer-down on 192 of 200 seeds.
V3-fired.player: visible: the response no longer opens fire on a holstered agent who fired before they came. Follows Sky's gang-shooting call (2026-11-04, 'the seal waits until the cell is seen') and the veteran's shot (route B's middle).

F2-before-final.note: The code is right and my lend page contradicted itself (F2 'never recalled' against 1.3 'the floor calls it back'). Read it as: a man who breaks in the final fight, or whose crew's car is gone, runs off holstered and never comes back. A crew that breaks before the final fight with its car still able to drive boards and drives off holstered, out of every fight while away, and comes back to block again after security.rivals.retreat (M059-3.5, 0.41.0; CrewBrokenPre clears on return). That keeps Sky's point that destroying the car is what ends them. Keel's report line 'out of every fight' holds only until the return.

our-car-ends.note: On the split nobody walks out (L8), so once both cars have left anyone still on the map can only be caught at the countdown: ending at once gives the same result sooner. With G1 (the Go waits for a Board in progress) and the Go's card naming who is left behind.

Q1.what: The quiet final fight's floor: 15 s or 10 s?
Q1.why: Route A's fight runs a median 13 s: Inez's warning lets four agents and the guard shoot first, from 6 m, so the crew breaks fast. Thinning route B's crew does the same (10-11 s). The 15 s floor was Aster's reading of your 'try the shorter' (2026-10-30).
options: a: floor 10 s (median 10-40 s, 95 % under 90 s): preparation earns a short fight
b: keep 15 s: Pulse makes the warned crew spring from cover (unmeasured, about +5-10 s), which takes some of the warning's value away

Q2.what: The veteran's price: Popovic out on about 6 seeds in 10, the other three caught on nearly all of them. Is that fair?
Q2.why: Shooting the rival car means gunfire, so the final fight is loud and the police come to Popovic's car in the bay (L6). The three beat them there, then have about 30 s to cross 64 m to our car before 8:10. Each caught agent is +4 Trail and a Talker test.
options: a: yes: possible, and far from free; the band becomes out 40-70 %, captures shown; Waymark tries driving our car round once the rival car is burnt
b: in a loud fight everyone at Popovic's car may ride in it (our car lost, +1 T, hunted): not proven yet
c: after Popovic is out, one police countdown (no 8:10 cap): all four out 3 -> 13 % of wins

Q3.what: Loud on route B: keep it the hard way (about 37 %), or make it a real route?
Q3.why: In a loud fight the police come for Popovic's car in the bay while the three are at the square. Loud by the front door already wins 66.5 %.
options: a: keep: the lend is the quiet route's tool, the book says the police come for his car if it goes loud
b: let everyone at his car ride in a loud fight (as Q2 b)
